difficulty_reason: H2: The author proves both implications: (i)=>(ii) by using compactness (prop:Ind-cpt) to factor arbitrary objects and morphisms of (h_C/X) through a common X_i and thus verify the two filteredness conditions plus cofinality, and (ii)=>(i) by prop:Yoneda-density together with prop:cofinally-small-sub.

core_obligations: for (i)=>(ii), given X = colim X_i and two objects phi: S -> X, phi': S' -> X of (h_C/X), uses prop:Ind-cpt to factor both through some X_i (replacing i by i' by filteredness), verifying the first filteredness condition
notes in passing that the canonical morphisms X_i -> X give a cofinal functor I -> (h_C/X), so (h_C/X) is cofinally small

for two morphisms f, g: S => S' over X, factors phi' through phi'_i: S' -> X_i and finds alpha: i -> j with X(alpha) phi'_i f = X(alpha) phi'_i g, drawing the diagram that equalizes f and g and concluding (h_C/X) is filtered
for (ii)=>(i) uses prop:Yoneda-density to write X as the colimit of (h_C/X) -> C^, then takes a cofinal full subcategory I via prop:cofinally-small-sub to present X as an ind-object
